core_noise.png: Toy states on a simulated IBM device noise model (FakeFez, q=1–3, fixed random sign states, three transpiler seeds, 4000 shots per circuit): (a) individual-seed raw/independent-readout-calibrated p1 with 95% percentile parametric bootstrap intervals from 2000 joint test/calibration resamples and ideal ticks shows that noise lifts same pairs above zero, breaking the one-sided single-1 guarantee and requiring a threshold; (b) actual level-1 all-to-all and level-3 FakeFez transpilations of random near pairs and one state preparation show exponential preparation cost with a qualitative one-expected-gate-fault guide from the FakeFez median 2q error (not a universal device limit); (c) independence and union-bound image false alarms for 4096 tiles mark directly measured f=p1(same) for the per-unit single-shot rule k=1, τ=0 (flag ones/k > τ), while the separate table designs minimal multi-shot k and τ using exact binomial tails at worst-seed raw p(same) and least-separated p(near) for ≤1% false alarm and ≥99% power per toy unit (q=1 uses orthogonal), conditional plug-in binomial calculations rather than validated image-level guarantees, and the independent-decision 1% image target f ≤ 2.4536923×10⁻⁶ is extrapolated, not measured, and unresolved by 4000 shots. Image false-alarm probability is 1−(1−f)^4096 under independence; f ≤ 0.01/4096 suffices by the union bound without independence. Noise was simulated in Aer with FakeFez and FakeBrisbane on toy q=1–3 states; F6 is simulation only; F8 separately reports toy states on ibm_marrakesh, a real IBM Heron r2 processor.
core_validation.png: F7 compares exact SWAP probabilities with finite-shot ideal Aer circuit estimates for the validation pairs; these ideal-simulator checks do not establish performance for toy states on a simulated IBM device noise model.
core_perceptual_ablation.png: Default v0.2 median + AC RMS cutoff 25 (t=0.65, 2048 shots) versus ablation AC > 10 (t=0.8, 4096 shots), selected using exactly E3's six calibration artworks, cases, constraints and tie-breaks. Panel (a) averages exact image flag probabilities over six held-out paintings, with benign cases above the divider and all eight content cases below (including tiny edits). Panel (b) reports the same cases and supplemental JPEG90 for synthetic seeds 0..15 (mean; cyclic donors), and each manifest stress image separately. Every cell uses exact binomial tails and the probability of any region flagging; no measurement sampling. Neither supplemental synthetics nor JPEG90 enters selection. Full-precision per-image data: core_perceptual_ablation_data.csv; artwork bootstrap intervals: ../results/core_perceptual_v3.json. The dead-zone removes the flat-region cliff: synthetic stress benign false alarm 37.78% to 0.157%; mean JPEG 90 false alarm over 16 synthetic seeds 62.93% to 0.059%. But held-out benign false alarm rises from 2.78% [95% CI 0.00%, 8.33%] to 14.09% [5.84%, 22.37%], while content detection rises from 65.14% [59.45%, 70.83%] to 72.95% [66.74%, 79.18%]. This did not generalise, so v0.2 remains the default; dead-zone is an ablation only. Historical E3 outputs are unchanged.
core_hardware.png: F8: toy states on ibm_marrakesh, a real IBM Heron r2 processor; job dbhlpatep8hs73amdun0, 2026-10-29T14:48:12.997571Z. 18 comparisons at 4000 shots per PUB, with 14 shared all-0/all-1 readout-calibration PUBs in the same job. Random sign states (state seed 2026), q=1,2,3; same, near (q>=2), orthogonal; ancilla and destructive; a q=2 Hadamard orthogonal control. ISA optimization level 3, transpiler seed 7. Hardware raw and independent-bit readout-corrected p1 have 95% percentile parametric-bootstrap intervals from 2000 joint test/calibration resamples. FakeFez raw predictions and their intervals are the three C2 routing seeds 7,23,91 from core_noise.csv, using the same toy-state seed; FakeFez is a different device and a stored noise snapshot, so this is an illustrative comparison, not validation of a noise model for Marrakesh. Ideal ticks and same-pair expanded panels are shown. Intervals condition on this run and exclude device drift, calibration-model error and routing variability. Noise breaks one-sided error, so a threshold is needed. Readout correction does not remove gate error. These are toy states; q=11 remains far beyond today's hardware. Reported QPU usage: 36 seconds (complete).
